porter: Use case: stylized-concept. Production asset: ONE completely new, uniquely identifiable ordinary customer portrait sprite for a Republican-era Shanghai pawnshop game, circa 1920s-1930s. Genuine transparent background, isolated single figure, no colored backdrop, no vignette, no ambient halo, no cast shadow outside body, no writing. Portrait aspect 2:3, whole head and both elbows completely inside image, frame from 8% empty space above head to mid thighs, 10% side margins. Natural human anatomy, proportionate head, waist at about 65% of image height. Restrained semi-realistic opaque gouache, visible confident brush planes, matte fabric and skin, muted old indigo/umber/gray-green. Soft warm light upper left; not photo, not shiny 3D, not anime. The face must be a distinct individual, not the usual worried middle-aged generic short-haired man with raised inner eyebrows and open mouth. Closed mouth, purposeful personal expression. No palm-out bargaining gesture and no pointing at viewer. Subject: Chinese male dock porter about 34, extremely dark sun-weathered brown skin on face, neck and arms, clearly much darker than all other townsfolk. Very broad short square face, flat wide cheekbones, wide nose bridge, small deeply-set narrow eyes, thick straight low brows, broad closed lips, compact ears. Almost shaved black buzzcut with visible scalp, no moustache or stubble. Squat powerful barrel chest, very thick neck and stocky functional muscular shoulders, ordinary laborer's proportions not bodybuilder. Pose: torso angled 25 degrees right, head turned to viewer, LEFT ELBOW raised strongly sideways while left hand presses a small coarse pale towel against left temple wiping sweat, face unobscured; RIGHT hand grips a short coil of carrying rope at the RIGHT side of his waist, no arm extended toward camera. Silhouette deliberately asymmetrical with one high elbow. Faded sleeveless dark indigo coarse vest, partly open neck, worn wide cloth waist sash, loose work trousers, a few sensible repairs, not covered in shredded tatters. Busy, tired, direct gaze with tightly set mouth.
